## A1

> One mind-moment at a time in a stream: *dve cittāni ekato nappavattanti*, "two cittas do not occur together", even for Buddhas. ⭐ Lifted 2026-09-30: in the Kathāvatthu it is a premise BOTH parties hold. The Theravādin's reductio "would two contacts … two cittas come together?" is refused by the opponent; the commentary identifies the two contacts as ear-contact and mind-contact

**`a1_never_together`** (Mind.lean)

```lean
def a1_never_together (S : Scale) (s : Stream S) : Prop := ∀ m n, m ≠ n → ¬ S.lt (s.arise n) (s.close m) ∨ ¬ S.lt (s.arise m) (s.close n)
```

*Blind reader:* For any two different moments m and n, at least one of: n does not arise before m closes, or m does not arise before n closes. No two different moments can overlap; touching is allowed (the test is strict less-than).

## A3

> Proximity (*anantara*): each moment conditions its immediate successor — *natthi etesaṃ antaraṃ*, "there is no interval between them" (the commentary), which it keeps apart from immediacy in TIME: across cessation there is none, and the condition still holds. ⚠️ Corrected 2026-10-13 (the Kv 8.2 control's vetting, F5): the clause "even across many thousands of kappas" and its line `abh05t.nrf.xml:2409` moved to ANSWERS Kv 8.2 — that line is the anuṭīkā's refutation of the intermediate existence (it ends *nattheva antarābhavo*); runs registered before keep their PREREG copies

**`a3_cit_labels_are_moments`** (Join.lean)

```lean
def a3_cit_labels_are_moments (S : Scale) (j : Joined S) : Prop :=
  ∀ i k a b m n, j.w.occs[i]? = some a → j.w.occs[k]? = some b → j.mom i = some m → j.mom k = some n → (a.cit = b.cit ↔ m = n)
```

*Blind reader:* For any two occurrences both assigned moments, they have equal cit label exactly when they are assigned the same moment.

**`a3_every_moment_has_an_occurrence`** (Join.lean)

```lean
def a3_every_moment_has_an_occurrence (S : Scale) (j : Joined S) : Prop := ∀ m, ∃ i, i < j.w.occs.length ∧ j.mom i = some m
```

*Blind reader:* Every moment of the stream is assigned to by some occurrence index within the occurrence list.

**`a3_no_moment_between`** (Mind.lean)

```lean
def a3_no_moment_between (S : Scale) (s : Stream S) : Prop := ∀ m n, s.prox m n ↔ (S.lt (s.arise m) (s.arise n) ∧ ∀ k, ¬ (S.lt (s.arise m) (s.arise k) ∧ S.lt (s.arise k) (s.arise n)))
```

*Blind reader:* For any m, n: prox m n holds exactly when m arises strictly before n and no moment at all arises strictly between them. prox is the immediate successor by arising time; if arising times are dense or tied it may be empty.

**`a3_proximity_is_the_streams_prox`** (Join.lean)

```lean
def a3_proximity_is_the_streams_prox (S : Scale) (j : Joined S) : Prop :=
  ∀ i k, (Condition.anantara, i, k) ∈ j.w.holds ↔ ∃ m n, j.mom i = some m ∧ j.mom k = some n ∧ j.s.prox m n
```

*Blind reader:* For all positions i, k: the triple (anantara, i, k) is in the holds list exactly when i and k map to moments m and n with prox m n: the anantara links match the stream's prox in both directions and require both positions to map to a moment.

## A4

> Most matter lasts **17** mind-moments: *rūpe dharanteyeva soḷasa cittāni uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, taṃ pana sattarasamena cittena saddhiṃ nirujjhati* (the two-walkers simile follows). ⚠️ CONTESTED in the tradition: the Mūlaṭīkā REPORTS an aṭṭhakathā figure of **16⅓** (*tatiyabhāgādhika-soḷasa*) and argues that the Vibhaṅga commentary's own rebirth passage (*vibha. aṭṭha.* 227) implies **16**. ⚠️ Tier corrected 2026-09-30: the 17 is COMMENTARIAL too (it was filed as sub-commentarial only). ⚠️ The Saṅgaha states it of "material dhammas" with no "most" (*sattarasa cittakkhaṇāni rūpadhammānamāyū*); the exceptions are the commentaries'

**`a4_life`** (Mat.lean)

```lean
def a4_life (m : Mat) : Prop :=
  ∀ k ∈ m.kalapas, (∀ r ∈ k.members, r ≠ .kayavinnatti ∧ r ≠ .vacivinnatti) → k.life = 51
```

*Blind reader:* Every kalapa whose members include neither bodily-intimation nor verbal-intimation matter has life exactly 51; clusters containing either are unconstrained.

**`a4_life_in_the_stream`** (Link.lean)

```lean
def a4_life_in_the_stream (S : Scale) (l : Link S) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, l.concrete k = true →
    (l.phase k = .arise → Steps l.s.prox 16 (l.mom k) (l.ceaseMom k) ∧ l.ceasePhase k = .dissolve) ∧
    (l.phase k = .stand → Steps l.s.prox 17 (l.mom k) (l.ceaseMom k) ∧ l.ceasePhase k = .arise) ∧
    (l.phase k = .dissolve → Steps l.s.prox 17 (l.mom k) (l.ceaseMom k) ∧ l.ceasePhase k = .stand)
```

*Blind reader:* For every concrete item: arising → reached by exactly 16 steps, cease phase dissolve; standing → 17 steps, cease phase arise; dissolving → 17 steps, cease phase stand (exact step counts).

**`a4_variant_sixteen`** (Occurs.lean)

```lean
def a4_variant_sixteen (S : Scale) (l : Link S) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, l.concrete k = true → l.phase k = .arise → Steps l.s.prox 15 (l.mom k) (l.ceaseMom k) ∧ l.ceasePhase k = .dissolve
```

*Blind reader:* For a link: for every concrete item that arises at a citta's arising, the cease moment is reached from the start moment in exactly 15 steps of proximity and the cease phase is dissolve. Vacuous if nothing is concrete and arising.

## A5

> The space element is *paricchedarūpa*: the delimitation between kalāpas, keeping them unmixed; it has no nature of its own (*anipphanna*). The Dhammasaṅgaṇī's space element is "space, the spatial, void, aperture, **untouched by the four great elements**". ⚠️ That Piṭaka line is READ TWO WAYS, and the Paramatthadīpanī records the dispute: the Atthasālinī and the Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā take it as unentangled space (*nijjaṭākāsa*, *ajaṭākāsa*); the ṭīkās take it as paricchedarūpa. So the lift to the Piṭaka holds only on the ṭīkās' reading (corrected 2026-09-30 by the refuter)

**`a5_space`** (Mat.lean)

```lean
def a5_space (m : Mat) : Prop :=
  ∀ g ∈ m.gaps, g.1 < m.kalapas.length ∧ g.2 < m.kalapas.length ∧ g.1 ≠ g.2
```

*Blind reader:* Every gap is a pair of two different valid kalapa indexes.

## A7

> Time (*kāla*) is designated on the occurrence of dhammas and is "a mere concept, not existing by its own nature" (*paññatto kālo … sabhāvato avijjamānattā paññattimattako*)

**`a7_reckoning_keeps_order`** (Clocks.lean)

```lean
def a7_reckoning_keeps_order (S R : Scale) (z : Reck S R) : Prop := ∀ a b, S.lt a b → ¬ R.lt (z.f b) (z.f a)
```

*Blind reader:* f never reverses order: if a is strictly below b in S, then f b is not strictly below f a in R (monotone, non-strict; f may be constant).

## A9

> **Delimiting space is CONDITIONED; the Kathāvatthu commentary classes the other two spaces as mere concepts.** It names three: delimiting space (*paricchedākāsa*), conditioned (the Saṅgaha has the space element arising from all four origins, A65); the space left by removing a kasiṇa and unentangled space (*ajaṭākāsa*), *paññattimattā*. The Kathāvatthu refutes "space is unconditioned"; the commentary gives the opponents' (Uttarāpathakas', Mahisāsakas') argument as "the two kinds are not conditioned, so space is unconditioned", so the debate turns on the concept-spaces. ⚠️ In §462 the Theravādin also declines "space is conditioned"; no commentary explains why, and reading it as "concepts are n …

**`a9_three_spaces`** (Status.lean)

```lean
def a9_three_spaces (c : Status) : Prop :=
  c.spaceSort .delimiting = .rupa ∧ c.spaceSort .kasina = .pannatti ∧ c.spaceSort .unentangled = .pannatti
```

*Blind reader:* delimiting maps to rupa, kasina maps to pannatti, unentangled maps to pannatti.

## A16

> The sun and moon discs travel ~42,000 yojanas up (half Sineru's height) and light three continents at one moment. ⚠️ **NOT at the same height: moon BELOW, sun ABOVE, one yojana between; 100 yojanas from the moon's lower edge to the sun's upper edge** (`:8353` — missed by the 2026-09-30 sun–moon pre-registration). ⭐ The ṭīkā: 42,000 holds "for the FIRST kappa" — later a few yojanas less, as the earth rises

**`a16_stack`** (Cosmos.lean)

```lean
def a16_stack (c : Cosmos) : Prop :=
  2 * c.moonBottom ≤ c.risen ∧ c.risen ≤ 2 * c.moonBottom + 200 ∧ c.sunBottom = c.moonBottom + c.moon.2.2 + 1 ∧ c.moonBottom + 100 = c.sunBottom + c.sun.2.2
```

*Blind reader:* Twice moonBottom is at most risen; risen is at most twice moonBottom plus 200; sunBottom equals moonBottom plus the moon's third component plus 1; and moonBottom plus 100 equals sunBottom plus the sun's third component (the last two force the two third components to sum to 99).

## A24

> The RATE of mind: in one finger-snap moment (*accharākkhaṇa*) "many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of cittas arise" (*anekāni cittakoṭisatasahassāni uppajjanti*: > 10¹² per snap); no single citta lasts a night or a day; quoted with the Milindapañha's measure (a cartload of rice-grains too few to count the cittas of one snap). The same rate for feeling: *vedanā … ekaccharakkhaṇe koṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā uppajjitvā nirujjhati* ⚠️ READ 2026-10-20 (correction 4 §1.2): the rate is encoded as *any trillion consecutive cittas with no cessation moment among them arise within one snap*, with 0 < snap < night ≤ week; a window-for-every-reading form would have forced a stream with no last moment.

**`a24_no_night`** (Clocks.lean)

```lean
def a24_no_night (S R : Scale) (z : Reck S R) : Prop :=
  ∀ m, R.lt (z.f (z.s.close m)) (R.add (z.f (z.s.arise m)) z.night)
```

*Blind reader:* For every moment m, f(close m) is strictly below f(arise m) + night: each moment's duration in R is less than "night".

**`a24_rate`** (Clocks.lean)

```lean
def a24_rate (S R : Scale) (z : Reck S R) : Prop :=
  ∀ m n, StepsFree z.cessation z.s.prox 1000000000000 m n → R.lt (z.f (z.s.arise n)) (R.add (z.f (z.s.arise m)) z.snap)
```

*Blind reader:* For any two moments m and n joined by exactly 10^12 stream steps, none departing from a moment flagged cessation, the clock time of n's arising is strictly less than m's arising time plus one snap.

## A28

> Citta has **89** types (54 sense-sphere, 15 fine-material, 12 immaterial, 8 supramundane), or **121** when each supramundane citta is reckoned by the five jhānas (8 × 5 = 40)

```lean
def a28_eightynine (t : Tax) : Prop :=
  t.kinds.Nodup ∧ t.kinds89.length = 89 ∧ num t.kinds89 (·.bhumi == .kama) = 54 ∧
  num t.kinds89 (·.bhumi == .rupa) = 15 ∧ num t.kinds89 (·.bhumi == .arupa) = 12 ∧ num t.kinds89 (·.bhumi == .lokuttara) = 8
```

*Blind reader:* The kinds list has no repeats; its collapsed version (kinds89) has 89 entries, split 54 kama, 15 rupa, 12 arupa and 8 lokuttara (lokuttara cittas differing only by jhana or feeling merge).

**`a28_onetwentyone`** (Tax.lean)

```lean
  ∀ c ∈ t.kinds89, c.bhumi = .lokuttara → ∀ n ∈ [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], ∃ k ∈ t.kinds, reckon89 k = c ∧ k.jhana = n
```

*Blind reader:* The kinds list has 121 entries, 40 of them lokuttara; for every lokuttara citta in kinds89 and each jhana number 1 to 5, some citta in kinds collapses to it and has that jhana number.

**`o_a28_every_type`** (Occurs.lean)

```lean
def o_a28_every_type (w : World S R) : Prop := ∀ c ∈ w.tax.kinds89, ∃ p ∈ w.proc.procs, ∃ s ∈ p.steps, reckon89 s.citta = c
```

*Blind reader:* Every item in the world's list of 89 kinds must appear in at least one process: some step of some process must have its citta reckoned (by reckon89) as that kind.

## A40

> One mind-moment is three sub-moments: arising, standing, dissolution (*uppādaṭhitibhaṅgavasena khaṇattayaṃ ekacittakkhaṇaṃ nāma*). ⚠️ Earlier than the manual: the Sammohavinodanī counts three sub-moments to every citta (*uppādaṭṭhitibhaṅgavasena tayo tayo khaṇā*), and the Visuddhimagga makes them EQUAL (*cittassa uppādakkhaṇopi ṭhitikkhaṇopi bhaṅgakkhaṇopi ekasadisā*) and matter's arising and dissolution moments equal to them

**`a40_three_equal`** (Mind.lean)

```lean
def a40_three_equal (S : Scale) (s : Stream S) : Prop := ∀ m, ∃ d, S.lt S.zero d ∧ s.stand m = S.add (s.arise m) d ∧ s.dissolve m = S.add (s.stand m) d ∧ s.close m = S.add (s.dissolve m) d
```

*Blind reader:* For every moment there is a positive step d with stand = arise + d, dissolve = stand + d, close = dissolve + d: four times evenly spaced by one positive amount. (Implies a117's ordering.)

```lean
def a46_javana_by_person (w : Proc) : Prop :=

```

## A47

> Within a life the six-door process, interspersed with bhavaṅga, continues **unbroken for the life-span** (*bhavaṅgantaritā yāvatāyukamabbocchinnā pavattati*). The Vibhāvinī supplies the exception the root leaves out: unbroken "when there is no cessation attainment" (*abbocchinnā asati nirodhasamāpattiyan*). So it does NOT collide with A111 (corrected 2026-09-30 by the refuter; the first version called it a collision)

**`a47_unbroken`** (Link.lean)

```lean
def a47_unbroken (S : Scale) (l : Link S) : Prop := ∀ m, ¬ l.death m → ∃ n, l.s.prox m n
```

*Blind reader:* For every moment m that is not marked a death moment, some moment n is linked from m by prox: every non-death moment has at least one successor. (Re-read 2026-10-20 after the definition was corrected; the first reading — *every* moment has a successor, forcing an endless stream — showed the first version too strong. The re-reader adds: existence only, not uniqueness or lateness; death moments are exempt but may have a successor; a world with no death marks is endless; marking every moment death makes it trivial — the death marks are constrained by A122 and A58 elsewhere.)

**`a47_unbroken_on_the_clock`** (Clocks.lean)

```lean
def a47_unbroken_on_the_clock (S R : Scale) (z : Reck S R) : Prop :=
  ∀ m n, ¬ z.cessation m → z.s.prox m n → ¬ R.lt (z.f (z.s.close m)) (z.f (z.s.arise n))
```

*Blind reader:* For every moment m not flagged cessation and its next moment n, the clock time of m's closing is not strictly less than the clock time of n's arising (no gap; overlap allowed).

## A77

> The twelve links span three periods (past: ignorance, formations; present: eight; future: birth, decay-and-death), with 20 modes, 3 connections, 4 groups, 3 rounds (defilement, kamma, result) and 2 roots (ignorance, craving). **The round is beginningless** (*anādikaṃ*). ⚠️ At its cited place *anādikaṃ* is the CONCLUSION of *iccevaṃ* ("thus"), drawn from "with the arising of the taints, ignorance arises" (`:2825`); it stays an axiom through assertions ELSEWHERE — the Theragāthā commentary in its own voice (*anādimati saṃsāre*) and the Visuddhimagga ṭīkā: "granted, in beginningless saṃsāra no one has a beginning; 'the first suffering, birth' is said of the aggregate-continuum of ONE existence" …

## A78

> The 24 conditions, enumerated: root, object, predominance, proximity, contiguity, co-nascence, mutuality, support, decisive support, pre-nascence, post-nascence, repetition, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, absence, disappearance, non-disappearance

**`a78_relata`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a78_relata {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  ∀ f ∈ w.holds, ∃ a b, ends w f.2.1 f.2.2 = some (a, b) ∧ admits (sangaha f.1) a.kind b.kind = true
```

*Blind reader:* Every fact of any condition must have two real ends, and the kinds of those ends must be admitted for the group that `sangaha` assigns to the condition. Facts pointing at nonexistent positions make it false.

**`o_a78_every_condition`** (Occurs.lean)

## A79

> Root (*hetu*): the roots condition the states associated with them and the matter those states originate

**`a79_root_scope`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a79_root_scope {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop := facts_between_occurrences w .hetu sameCittaTogether
```

*Blind reader:* For every hetu fact, the ends have the same `cit` and rise time.

## A80

> Object (*ārammaṇa*): visible form conditions eye-consciousness, and so on for each sense; the five sense objects condition the mind-element; **any dhamma can condition mind-consciousness**. Whatever a citta arises taking as object conditions it

**`a80_object_sense`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a80_object_sense {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  facts_between_occurrences w .arammana fun a b =>
    ∀ r n d, a.rupa = some r → senseOfObject r = some n → (b.citta.map (·.dhatu)) = some (FormalAbhidhamma.Dhatu.sense d) → d = n
```

*Blind reader:* For every arammana fact, take the first end's rupa r with a sense number n; if the second end's citta has dhatu `sense d`, then d = n. Vacuous when the first end has no rupa, the rupa has no number, or the second end's dhatu is not a sense one.

## A81

> Predominance (*adhipati*): the four predominants (desire, energy, citta, investigation) condition their associated states and the matter they originate; so does whatever is esteemed as object

**`a81_predominance`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a81_predominance {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  ∀ f ∈ w.holds, f.1 = .adhipati → ∃ a b, ends w f.2.1 f.2.2 = some (a, b) ∧
    (sameCittaTogether a b ∨ (b.kind = .nama ∧ (Condition.arammana, f.2.1, f.2.2) ∈ w.holds))
```

*Blind reader:* Every predominance fact has endpoints such that either they are the same-citta-together case, or the second is of kind nama and an object fact on the same pair is also recorded. Fails if endpoints cannot be found.

## A82

> Contiguity (*samanantara*): the same relata as proximity, each citta to the next. ⚠️ That proximity, contiguity, absence and disappearance relate one and the same pair (the citta that has just ceased, the present one) is the Saṅgaha's GROUPING (ch. 8 §16), a computation from the definitions, held out with it: [ANSWERS](ANSWERS.md) "Saṅgaha ch. 8 grouping"

**`a82_contiguity_same_relata`** (Cond.lean)

```lean

  ∀ i j, (Condition.anantara, i, j) ∈ w.holds ↔ (Condition.samanantara, i, j) ∈ w.holds
```

*Blind reader:* For all i and j, an anantara fact (i,j) is present exactly when a samanantara fact (i,j) is present.

## A83

> Co-nascence (*sahajāta*): the four mental aggregates condition one another, as do the four great elements, and **mind and matter at conception**; citta and cetasikas condition mind-born matter; the great elements condition derived matter; matter conditions mind "at one time, and at another not"

**`a83_co_nascent`** (Cond.lean)

```lean

```

*Blind reader:* For every sahajata fact, the two ends have the same rise time. It says nothing about fall times.

## A84

> Mutuality (*aññamañña*): the four mental aggregates, the four great elements, and mind-and-matter at conception each condition the others. ⚠️ OURS: this relation is symmetric, so conditioning as a whole is not a partial order. It is not the only cycle: the heart-base conditions the mental aggregates by pre-nascence and they condition it by post-nascence, "helpers of their helper", which the Mūlaṭīkā denies is mutuality. Proximity is one strict order among several one-way conditions (pre-nascence, post-nascence, repetition)

**`a84_mutual`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a84_mutual {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  (facts_between_occurrences w .annamanna fun a b => a.rise = b.rise) ∧
  ∀ f ∈ w.holds, f.1 = .annamanna → (Condition.annamanna, f.2.2, f.2.1) ∈ w.holds
```

*Blind reader:* For every annamanna fact, the ends have the same rise time. Also, the reversed fact (annamanna, j, i) must be in the list.

*Blind reader:* At every sense moment, both the base and the object exist and each is present at the moment's arising. Its base half duplicates a116.

## A88

> Post-nascence (*pacchājāta*): **citta and cetasikas arising later support this body, which arose before them**. Not retrocausation, and the texts say so themselves: the Vibhāvinī raises the objection (*kathaṃ pana … pacchājātassa paccayatā?*) and answers that it supports a body still present; it sustains, it does not produce (the vulture-chicks' bodies kept by their wish for food, Paṭṭhāna-aṭṭhakathā); post-nascence is one of the five kinds of presence condition (ch. 8 §34). ⚠️ Separately, the Paṭṭhāna does let FUTURE dhammas condition present ones as OBJECT (knowledge of the future, `abh03m8.mul.xml:14089`) — and by predominance and by decisive support, natural decisive support included; th …

**`a88_post_born`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a88_post_born {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  facts_between_occurrences w .pacchajata fun a b => S.lt b.rise a.rise ∧ S.lt a.rise b.fall
```

*Blind reader:* Every post-born fact: the second arises strictly before the first arises, and the first arises strictly before the second falls.

## A89

> Repetition (*āsevana*): earlier wholesome states condition later wholesome ones, unwholesome unwholesome, functional functional (the javana run)

**`a89_repetition`** (Cond.lean)

```lean
def a89_repetition {S : Scale} (w : CondW S) : Prop :=
  facts_between_occurrences w .asevana fun a b =>
    a.kind = .nama ∧ b.kind = .nama ∧ S.lt a.rise b.rise ∧
    (a.citta.map (·.jati)) = (b.citta.map (·.jati)) ∧ (a.citta.map (·.jati)) ≠ some FormalAbhidhamma.Jati.vipaka ∧ a.citta.isSome = true
```

*Blind reader:* For every asevana fact, both ends are nama, the first rises strictly before the second, both have the same `jati`, that `jati` is not vipaka, and the first has a citta.

## A90

> Kamma: wholesome or unwholesome kamma conditions the resultant aggregates and kamma-born matter, **across time** (*nānākkhaṇika*, the Paṭṭhāna's own word in its detailed section); volition conditions its associated states and their matter at the same time ⚠️ No stored trace: the Kathāvatthu rejects *kammūpacaya*, an accumulation distinct from kamma that would stand "like a seed until the result arises"

**`a90_kamma`** (Cond.lean)

```lean

```

*Blind reader:* For every kamma fact: either the ends share `cit` and rise time; or the first rises strictly before the second and the second either has a vipaka citta or has `born` = kamma.
